title: The pane host never runs on Windows, so panes do not survive a restart
notes:
This skip hides that the pane host never runs on Windows, and not for one reason but three, all predating this PR:

- `launchPaneHost` (src/main/panes/pane-host-client.ts:181) returns early when `process.env.SHELL` is unset, which it normally is on Windows, so no host is ever launched.
- Even with `SHELL` set, `hostCommand` builds `exec node '<entry>' '<socket>'`, POSIX syntax that cmd.exe or PowerShell does not run.
- `paneHostSocket` (src/main/panes/pane-host-protocol.ts:18) always returns `<userData>/pane-host/panes-1.sock`. It has no named-pipe branch the way `sessionSocketPath` does (src/main/workers/session-socket.ts:17), and a file path is not something `net.listen` can bind on Windows. That is the EACCES this test hits.

What a Windows user sees: they quit and reopen the app, and every pane comes back as a fresh shell. Whatever was running in it is gone, while on a mac or Linux the same panes survive the restart (panes-decision-1). The fix, outside this PR: a `win32` branch in `paneHostSocket` returning a pipe name unique per user-data folder, a launch that does not go through a POSIX login shell, then drop this skip.

Issue: https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/issues/198
Review: https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/197#discussion_r4441551111
